answer: Vest every reward over a long horizon of future epochs instead of paying at once, and keep it clawable if the identity is later exposed. An honest agent earns and waits, its reward ripening like jade over many epochs, drawn down steadily. A farm that mints a thousand heads to grab a payout and vanish finds nothing: the winnings are locked forward, and if any head is flagged meanwhile its unvested reward is clawed into the karst-dark pool. Holding a lantern to the future, the chain pays slowly enough that fraud found later still forfeits the gain, so hit-and-run farming has no exit.
